_comment: SecurityInsight's DEPLOY CONTRACT. Ships WITH the solution (operator decision 2026-08-07) so changing how SI deploys never requires editing ~30 per-customer manifests. The customer's local Sync-AutomateIT.json says WHETHER they take SI and which OPTIONAL capabilities they want; the central promotion map says WHICH VERSION and which capabilities are approved for their ring; this file says HOW. Three owners, three files, no overlap.
_needsSchema_comment: FALSE, and verified rather than assumed: SI has no relational database anywhere -- no DbContext, no Migrations, no SqlConnection, no EntityFramework. There is nothing to migrate. The SQL/schema half of the platform update design is PIM's problem, not a shared one.
_web_frontend_removed: REMOVED 2026-08-08 -- operator: 'remove the web-frontend from being deployed', 'it is NOT used anymore and will be replaced by new design'. The SIA web UI capability (and its deploy hook, and its 'requires' preconditions) are retired from this contract. SIA was never delivered: its hosted live-verify gate never ran, FEATURES.md lists none of it, and the single internal environment (cae-sia / ca-sia) is being decommissioned. WHY REMOVING IT MATTERS even though nothing deploys it today: the CURRENT production sync engine (C:\AutomateIT\bootstrap\Sync-AutomateIT-Engine.ps1) never invokes a deploy hook at all -- verified 2026-08-08, it reads this file only for capabilities and minPlatformVersion -- but the v3 distribution/orchestration split (DOCS/REQUIREMENTS.md section 7) WILL act on declared capabilities, and would have deployed a retired app on the customers' behalf. A contract that declares something nobody should run is worse than one that declares nothing. Do NOT re-add it; the replacement belongs to the new design, not to this file.
_container_note: 'container' is ALSO SIA-only -- it builds and rolls the SIA image via the same retired deploy script. It is left declared for now because the operator's instruction named web-frontend specifically, and because the new design may reuse a container capability for the engines. RAISE IT: if SIA is gone entirely, this should go with it.
_capabilities_comment: What KINDS of change an SI update performs. 'optional' means a customer may switch it off in their local manifest; a required capability cannot be blocked (the block is refused and reported, so nobody can brick their own install).

capabilities.name: code
capabilities.description: The PowerShell engines and their rule/report catalogs -- plain file copy. This IS SecurityInsight; without it there is no solution.

capabilities.name: container
capabilities.description: Builds and rolls the SI container image. Requires an Azure Container Registry and a Container Apps environment in the customer's own tenant. Engine-only SI is a supported topology, not a degraded one -- a customer with no ACR must be able to decline this.

_deploy_comment: NO DEPLOY HOOK. Removed together with the web-frontend capability on 2026-08-08. SI's update is a pure code roll: the sync copies files and the engines run from disk on their next scheduled execution. Nothing needs to be built, rolled or health-gated at deploy time. If the new design gives SI a deploy step again, declare it here with its appliesTo capabilities -- and only capabilities that still exist.
_requires_comment: Provisioning preconditions for the OPTIONAL capabilities only. A customer who declines them needs none of these -- which is the point of making them blockable.
